Southern Nigeria Protectorate.fact: Egerton became Governor of Lagos Colony, covering most of the Yoruba lands in the southwest of what is now Nigeria, in 1903. The colonial office wanted to amalgamate the Lagos Colony with the protectorate of Southern Nigeria, and in August 1904 also appointed Egerton as High Commissioner for the Southern Nigeria Protectorate.

Southern Nigeria Protectorate.question: As early as 1908, _____ supported the idea of "a properly organized Agricultural Department with an energetic and experienced head", and the Department of Agriculture came into being in 1910
Southern Nigeria Protectorate.fact: Egerton was a strong advocate of colonial development. As early as 1908, Egerton supported the idea of "a properly organized Agricultural Department with an energetic and experienced head", and the Department of Agriculture came into being in 1910.

Southern Nigeria Protectorate.question: In 1912, _____ was replaced by Frederick Lugard, who was appointed Governor-General of both Southern and Northern Nigeria with the mandate to unite the two
Southern Nigeria Protectorate.fact: Egerton himself did not always approve of these policies, and they were not strictly upheld. The legal relationship between the Lagos government and the Yoruba states of the Lagos Colony was not clear, and it was not until 1908 that Egerton persuaded the Obas to accept the establishment of the Supreme Court in the main towns.

Southern Nigeria Protectorate.question: From 1914 to 1919, _____ was made Governor General of the now combined Colony of Nigeria
Southern Nigeria Protectorate.fact: Lugard returned to Nigeria as Governor of the two protectorates. From 1914 to 1919, Lugard was made Governor General of the now combined Colony of Nigeria.
